title: Integral proper base change on localizing categories
statement:
For a cartesian square with $p:X\to Y$ proper, $g:Y'\to Y$, $p':X'\to Y'$ and
$g':X'\to X$, the base change map $g^*Rp_*\to Rp'_*g'^*$ is an isomorphism of
functors $\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))\to\Loc(\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E))$.

proof.text: Use the standing scheme and coefficient setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: the four schemes are separated of finite type over a field of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, the arrows are morphisms over that field, and $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ is finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$. For $K\in\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral] states that the canonical ordinary proper base-change map $\beta_K:g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism. Its clause (1) places $Rp_*K$ in $\Dbc(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; [sk-lem-integral-models] (3) preserves $\Dbc$ under $g^*$ and $g'^*$, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b) gives properness of $p'$, so the same clause (1) for $p'$ places the other endpoint in $\Dbc(Y',\mathcal O_E)$. Thus the transformation to be extended is already invertible on the bounded constructible generators, with the ordinary module-object coefficients and ordinary inverse images used in the statement.

source.place: Proof paragraph, first sentence (invertibility on Dbc), using the existing stronger integral theorem; its blueprint proof, clause (3), supplies the finite-reduction and derived-completeness argument.

proof.text: By [det-proper-image-localizing-proper], proper direct image with $\mathcal O_E$ coefficients in the standing setting restricts to an exact sum-preserving functor on $\Loc(\Dctf)$. Properness of $p'$ follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b). Apply [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] to $g$ and $g'$ to obtain the corresponding exact sum-preserving inverse images. Composing these restrictions gives exact sum-preserving functors $g^*Rp_*$ and $Rp'_*g'^*$ from the source localizing category to the target one. The equality $\Dctf(T,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ in [sk-lem-integral-models] applies at every corner. Their localizing closures coincide directly from [sk-def-localizing-closure]: the collections of full replete triangulated subcategories containing the generators and closed under ambient sums are identical. Thus the source and target of both functors are exactly those stated in the item.

source.place: Proof paragraph, second sentence: exactness and direct-sum preservation on the localizing categories

proof.text: For every edge $u$, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] (1) identifies $u^{-1}\mathcal O_{E,T}$ with $\mathcal O_{E,T'}$, and its final paragraph makes module pullback exact. The coefficient maps come from pullback from the same point: the two routes around the square identify the pullback with the same coefficient sheaf. This is the ringed square required by [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies $Lu^*$ with $D(u^*)$, the functor induced by applying $u^*$ in every degree. The module pullback is the ringed-topos tensor pullback by [def-sfb-module-upper-star], and its adjunction is the usual tensor/inverse-image Hom bijection explicitly given in [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Thus these are the same module pullbacks and adjunctions used in both exchange formulas.

source.place: Proof paragraph, second sentence: exactness and direct-sum preservation on the localizing categories

proof.text: Check the underived composition comparison by its defining adjunction. For composable $h:Z\to W$, $k:W\to V$, the tensor pullback formula of [def-sfb-module-upper-star] cancels the intervening coefficient extension, giving the canonical isomorphism $(kh)^*M\cong h^*k^*M$. Under the two Hom bijections of [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction], a map $h^*k^*M\to N$ becomes $M\to k_*h_*N$; under the single bijection it becomes $M\to(kh)_*N$. The two are related by the pushforward composition of [def-sfb-module-lower-star-comp]: on underlying sheaves this is restriction along $(V_0\times_VW)\times_WZ\cong V_0\times_VZ$, as specified in [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp]. Hence the conjugate of the canonical tensor comparison is precisely that pushforward composition. The bijection in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] and the defining uniqueness in [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp] identify the tensor comparison with the latter node's $b$. This is an unpacking of the displayed Hom formulas and uniqueness, not a separate comparison theorem.

source.place: Proof paragraph, second sentence: exactness and direct-sum preservation on the localizing categories

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], on a K-flat resolution with flat terms the derived comparison $c_{h,k}$ is the class of the termwise canonical module comparison. Its coefficient-compatibility hypothesis was checked in step 3. Step 4 identifies this module comparison with [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. The exact-functor identification of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] therefore identifies the two derived comparisons: both are represented by the same chain map on the same resolution. Applying this to $(p',g)$ and $(g',p)$ identifies $\theta_\square$ of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] with the termwise $\theta$ in the extension lemma. The adjunctions are the derived adjunctions of the same module pullbacks and pushforwards [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Consequently the stated exchange is exactly
$$\beta_K=Rp'_*g'^*(\varepsilon_{p,K})\circ Rp'_*(\theta_{Rp_*K})\circ\eta_{p',g^*Rp_*K}.$$
This checks the actual morphism, including its unit and counit, before applying localizing extension.

source.place: Proof paragraph, second sentence: exactness and direct-sum preservation on the localizing categories

proof.text: Apply [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-extension] with $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ and the given cartesian square. Its scheme setting and admissible coefficient hypotheses are those fixed in step 1. It specifies the very same base-change map as step 5: the unit for $p'$, the canonical comparison of the two composed pullbacks, and the counit for $p$, in that order. In particular its conclusion concerns the stated canonical morphism. By the opening assertion of [sk-lem-integral-models], $\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E)=\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$, so step 1 proves invertibility on every generator required in that lemma's hypothesis. Its conclusion gives invertibility on $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\mathcal O_E))=\Loc(\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E))$. Together with the restricted functor types from step 2, this proves the claimed isomorphism of functors. The extension lemma states the result for this specified exchange transformation; no inference from mere naturality to shift compatibility is needed.

source.place: Final two sentences: extension by localizing determination, using the existing generic extension lemma in the explicitly cited proper-base-change-unbounded unit.
